quizData.question: The `<video>` element is a void element and cannot contain other elements.
quizData.explanation: `<video>` is a container element; it can hold `<source>` tags and fallback content.

slides.title: Video Attributes 🎚️
slides.content:
# Fine‑Tune Playback

- `autoplay` – starts playing automatically (often blocked by browsers unless muted).
- `loop` – repeats the video.
- `muted` – starts with no sound.
- `poster` – an image shown before the video plays.
- `preload` – hints to the browser: `none`, `metadata`, or `auto`.

Example:
```html
<video controls autoplay muted loop poster="thumbnail.jpg">
  ...
</video>
```

slides.title: Embedding a YouTube Video (iframe)
slides.content: Often you'll embed videos from platforms using an `<iframe>` instead of hosting yourself:
slides.codeSnippet:
<iframe width="560" height="315"
  src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/dQw4w9WgXcQ"
  title="YouTube video player"
  allowfullscreen></iframe>

slides.title: Accessibility for Media ♿
slides.content:
# Make Multimedia Usable for All

- For `<video>`, provide **captions** using the `<track>` element.
- Always include a descriptive `title` on `<iframe>` embeds.
- For audio, consider a transcript link.

```html
<video controls>
  <source src="video.mp4" type="video/mp4">
  <track kind="subtitles" src="captions.vtt" srclang="en" label="English">
</video>
```
Captions help deaf/hard‑of‑hearing users and improve engagement.

quizData.question: Which element provides text tracks (subtitles) for a video?
quizData.explanation: `<track>` specifies timed text tracks like subtitles, captions, or descriptions.
